A week of orbs, personas and settings you can actually search. That is this release.

0.5.3 shipped 15 September. Since then 48 pull requests landed on `develop` and none of them reached a user, because `main` — the branch every installer is built from — has not moved. That includes the fix this release exists to ship: CB-118 corrected the URL a screenshot-comment image is built from, and it has been sitting merged and reported done for four days while doing nothing at all, because `publish-screenshots.yml` is a `workflow_run` workflow and GitHub always runs the copy on the *default* branch — `main` — regardless of what `develop` holds. It only looks fixed because this repository happens to be public right now; the moment it is private again, every screenshot image in every PR comment 404s for a human reading it in a browser.

Still a beta. What follows is a large batch — see *Known limitations* for what has and has not been run on a real machine.

## New: orbs for sessions running in Anthropic's cloud

A Claude Code session running in Anthropic's cloud now draws an orb beside your local ones, with its real state, a context ring, and its post-turn summary on hover (CB-164). Clicking it opens the session in your browser; the flyout's keyboard button opens a read-only transcript panel. Off by default.

## New: paired machines mirror Codex, Grok, and personas

A paired machine's Codex and Grok sessions now mirror over the direct peer link the same way its Claude Code sessions already did (CB-162), and a mirrored session draws wearing its own persona — name, portrait and voice — resolved on the machine that owns the `CLAUDE.md`, never guessed from a path shared between two machines that happen to check the same project out in the same place (CB-163).

## New: a speaker mode for a reply too long to listen to

The speaker button gains a mode. **Full response** reads everything the assistant said, same as always. **Vibe code summary** asks a separate, throwaway `claude -p --model haiku` process for two or three sentences instead — a different process, a different conversation, nothing written into your transcript (CB-165). A short reply is read in full either way; summarizing one that's already brief would buy silence for nothing.

## New: fold a settings section, or just search for it

The settings window had grown to thirteen sections in one long scrolling column. Every section now folds and remembers how you left it, and a filter box at the top narrows the whole page to whatever you type (CB-166). Everything is expanded on a fresh install, so first launch looks exactly as it did before.

## New: a global hotkey to hide every orb at once

Ctrl+Alt+H (Windows) toggles every orb hidden or visible from anywhere, with the binding built to take more hotkeys later (CB-155). Uses Carbon on macOS specifically because it needs no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission.

## New: pinned chat panels survive a restart

A panel you pin now remembers that it's pinned, and where you left it, across quitting and relaunching the app (CB-111) — the persistence CB-110's own description asked for and didn't yet have.

## New: Claude Buddy comes back after a crash

Nothing shipped by this repo brought the app back if it crashed, on either platform (CB-49). macOS gets a `launchd` `KeepAlive` agent; Windows gets a Scheduled Task triggered off the OS's own Application Error event. Opt-in, gated behind the existing "Serve on launch" setting — a keep-alive that returns after every exit, including a deliberate quit, is the "app that will not stay quit" the ticket itself warns against.

## Fixed

- Screenshot comment images no longer 404 for a human with full read access to a private repo (CB-118) — see above for why this alone did not take effect until now.
- The fork-PR lookup `publish-screenshots.yml` runs against no longer matches nothing (CB-117).
- An `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` persona no longer needs unwrapping, and generated personas stay out of git.
- Windows background-orb clicks work, and a background Claude Code attach resolves `Claude.exe` correctly.
- An unattributed room turn draws no chip; a repeated message and a quoted one both survive in a room instead of one eating the other (CB-32, CB-33).
- A failed send keeps what you typed instead of clearing the composer (CB-35).
- Orb arrangement no longer relocates every orb just because one ended (CB-161); scroll-to-end settles once the extent actually stops moving instead of after two ticks (CB-160).
- A picture drawn by both an inline block and its delivery mirror no longer duplicates (CB-98).
- iTerm2/Terminal.app is asked to run a command instead of being handed a script file to open (CB-80).
- A stuck OpenClaw conversation nobody is looking at is let go instead of held forever (CB-92); a failed avatar decode is retried instead of cached as a permanent failure; a delivered message live-updates the open chat panel (CB-95).
- The Voice and Avatar fields in a settings table row are scoped to the persona section they belong to (CB-145).
- A session can no longer be ended out from under the background daemon it's hosting.
- Duplicate-launch handling exits cleanly instead of aborting the dispatcher (CB-178); Claude Buddy's own internal CLI processes no longer draw a stray orb for themselves.
- An unknown tmux pane owner is no longer treated as a mismatch; an attached-but-unaimable tmux client no longer opens a second tab (CB-158).
- The account app's own default-account jobs are asked for even when this instance inherited a different account already running (CB-114).
- The OpenClaw receive loop runs on its own thread instead of borrowing the thread pool, closing a concurrency hang at handshake.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.4-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.4-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.4-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.5.4-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the right one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or `Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.5.3-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged, so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Local Network permission does not.** Same CDHash rule as every prior release: replacing the app loses the grant, and paired machines plus an OpenClaw gateway start failing with `No route to host`. Approve it again in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network. A headless Mac still cannot; pair from the machine with a screen and add the headless one by address.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and leaves your hook configuration alone.

Crash keep-alive and the global hide-orbs hotkey are both off/default until you turn them on — keep-alive under the existing "Serve on launch" setting, the hotkey works out of the box as Ctrl+Alt+H (Windows) with no setting yet to remap it.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click **Install Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave the hook checkboxes ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"** too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code, Codex, and Grok each run. Until it's wired in, the app starts and runs correctly and shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them. Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than duplicating.

## Known limitations

Everything below is named because it was not measured, not because it is expected to fail.

- **Cloud session orbs are unverified on Windows**, and on the account they were built against, the feature draws exactly one orb — most rows in a real roster are local sessions registered for remote control, not cloud sessions, and that is the feature working correctly rather than a bug.
- **Paired Codex/Grok mirroring and persona-over-the-wire have not had live cross-machine smoke testing.** The release unit, integration and UI suites are green; a real paired macOS/Windows Codex or Grok session pending manual confirmation.
- **The vibe code summary's round trip runs 6–7 seconds** on the one machine it was measured on, and it does not fall back to the full response on failure — it says so in one sentence instead, by design.
- **Whether the global hotkey actually fires on a real running app has not been confirmed on either platform** from this pipeline; the registry, parsing and settings round-trip are unit-tested, but registering and receiving an OS-level hotkey needs a real window-server session no headless run has.
- **Windows personas, Windows cloud orbs, and Windows crash keep-alive have not been run** against a live install on that OS. CI runs the parse and UI tests on both legs.
- **Local Network consent is lost on every upgrade**, same as every prior release.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info → Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.
